Automatic water level monitor and pump control


Use a BMP,180 pressure sensor to measure the water level in a tank. Put the sensor inside a small plastic container, invert the container, and immerse it into the bottom of the tank. The air pocket in the container will ensure that the sensor does not get wet, but will experience the air pressure increase caused by the water level.



Default sensor is set to BMP180


If you have connected any other sensor(BMP/BME280, MS5611)

  1. Click the scan button
  2. Check that your sensor is shown
  3. Select the pressure parameter (default is temperature 🌡️)


Automatically Scan and allow the user to select a sensor


In this experiment we shall use a user input block which scans the I2C port for supported sensors, and shows the user a list of detected sensors to select from.


The parameters supported by the selected Sensor are automatically fed into the adjacent drop-down menu for the user to select.


Logic


If pressure is below a certain level, it means the tank is empty. So the motor must turn on. This is done by connecting a relay to PB0 . PB0 is made HIGH (5V)


If pressure exceeds a certain level, tank is full. So turn off the motor via the relay. PB0 is made LOW (0V)






connections for I2C sensors


Sensors which use the I2C communication interface require 4 connections to be made.


  • VCC ( Can be 5V or 3.3V). The 4 wire sensor cable has 5V, and most commonly available sensors have a 3.3V regulator on board to convert the voltage .
  • GND . Ground
  • SCl. Clock pin. Internally pulled up to 5V via 10K resistor. PC0
  • SDA . Data . Internally pulled up to 5V via 10K. PC1
